text:
A: Alright? Can you hear me, yeah?
B: Hi. Yes, I can hear you. I'm Maricel.
A: Lewis. Nice one. So, er, what d'you do?
B: I'm a pharmacy technician. In Leyton.
A: Oh, right. My mum works at a GP surgery. Practice manager.
B: Oh, okay. So she knows all about the prescription side, then.
A: Yeah, she moans about it, to be fair. Every dinner it's someone who's shouted at the receptionist.
B: That happens to us as well. It's always the person in the middle. And you, what do you do?
A: I've got my own business. Tiling. Bathrooms, kitchen floors, splashbacks, that kind of thing.
B: Oh, tiling. That's actually interesting. I do pottery, so I'm sort of obsessed with glazes. Do you ever do handmade tiles? Or is it mostly the big shiny ones?
A: Mostly the big ones, yeah. Porcelain, big format, people love it now. Had one woman wanted handmade Moroccan ones once. Nightmare. None of 'em are the same size, you can't get your lines straight.
B: But that's the point of them! They're meant to be a bit uneven.
A: Yeah, try telling the grout that. Took me twice as long. Charged her for it, mind.
B: Ha. Fair enough, I suppose. When we went to Lisbon, all the buildings had those painted blue tiles. Azulejos. I spent the whole time taking photos of walls. My partner thought I'd gone mad.
A: Lisbon. Is that Portugal, yeah? I've only done the Algarve. Albufeira, with the lads.
B: Mm. Different sort of trip, maybe.
A: Ha, yeah, bit different. Didn't see many walls. Saw a lot of the pool bar.
B: Erm, so are you busy, with the business?
A: Yeah, it's alright. Bits and bobs. I sort of pick my jobs. Word of mouth mostly, my dad knows a lot of people.
B: That's good, that you don't have to advertise. I sell a few mugs on Instagram, but honestly, it's so much work. Taking the photos, the posting, the packaging. You make maybe five pounds a mug after everything.
A: Five quid? You want to charge more. Have you seen what they sell mugs for in them fancy shops? Thirty quid, some of 'em. Just price it for whoever's buying.
B: Erm, I don't know. I don't want it to be only for rich people.
A: Nah, I'm just saying. People pay for handmade, don't they.
B: Mm. Maybe. Do you live in Bishop's Stortford?
A: Yeah. Back at my parents' for a bit, just while I save up. It's twenty minutes from Stansted, so that's a bonus.
B: I'm in Walthamstow. The overground's rammed every morning. I'd love twenty minutes from anywhere.
A: Ha, yeah, the M11's no better, mate. Sat on it for forty minutes Tuesday.
B: So, erm, what do you do when you're not working?
A: Football, mostly. Spurs, five-a-side on a Wednesday, bit of FC on the PlayStation. Golf with my dad sometimes, but I'm rubbish, I just get wound up.
B: I don't really know anything about football, honestly. I couldn't name a Spurs player.
A: You've heard of Harry Kane, though, surely?
B: Yes, okay, I know Harry Kane. Isn't he—
